customer_question: We don't have finalized versions of the compliance folder documents yet -- can we submit drafts, a reused diagram, or simple photos instead, and replace them later?
question_variants: Can we use a draft operation manual since our spec isn't finalized yet?
Can we substitute the module's own block diagram for our product block diagram?
Can scaled photos of the product stand in for a formal outline drawing?
actual_issue: The customer had not yet finalized several of the product documents needed for the compliance folder (operation manual, product block diagram, product outline drawing) and needed to know what level of fidelity or formality was acceptable, given that the underlying product specification was still in development.
plain_english_explanation: The compliance folder needs certain product documents, but they don't have to be the polished, final versions before the registration can move forward. A rough draft of the manual, the module's own diagram standing in for a dedicated product diagram, and simple photos with a ruler in frame instead of a formal technical drawing are all acceptable, on the understanding that anything still in draft form gets swapped out for the final version later.
consultant_answer: For the operation manual, the document does not need to be at the level of what ships with the product -- a draft manuscript or even memo-level document is acceptable. For the product block diagram, if the customer doesn't have one ready, the module's own block diagram (taken from the module's datasheet) can be reused in its place. For the product outline drawing, a front-view and side-view photograph of the actual product with a ruler or scale included alongside it is acceptable in place of a formal dimensional drawing. When the customer subsequently submitted a draft operation manual PDF (with the product specification not yet finalized, on the understanding it would be replaced later), the module's own block diagram, and photographs for the outline requirement, all three were accepted as sufficient to build the compliance folder.
decision_logic: Compliance folder documents are accepted at a practical, not necessarily final, level of fidelity: a draft or memo-level operation manual, a reused module-level block diagram in place of a dedicated product diagram, and simple scaled photographs in place of a formal outline drawing are all acceptable substitutes when the customer's own finalized materials are not yet available, with replacement expected once final versions exist.
final_recommendation: When a customer cannot yet provide finalized compliance folder documents, offer the practical substitutes that are generally acceptable: a draft or memo-level operation manual, the module's own block diagram in place of a dedicated product diagram, and scaled front/side photographs in place of a formal outline drawing, with the expectation that finalized versions will replace drafts later.
risk_if_done_wrong: Insisting on fully finalized compliance documents before proceeding would unnecessarily delay compliance folder assembly and registration closeout in situations where acceptable, lower-fidelity substitutes would have sufficed.
